subject.title: [RFC] Agent Teleconference — minimum-viable scoped meeting primitive with working prototype

question: Should OpenClaw accept a core agent teleconference lifecycle primitive now, and if so what storage, authorization, and handoff boundary should it use?
rationale: The feature is plausible and already scoped by discussion, but it adds new CLI/API verbs, persistent cross-agent state, transcript privacy implications, and config surface that automation cannot safely choose.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow core design first
options.body: Define the smallest core lifecycle API, SQLite or named-artifact storage model, transcript policy, and tests before inviting an implementation PR.

options.title: Route to plugin/API exploration
options.body: Ask for a plugin or plugin-API gap proposal if maintainers want the core to expose seams rather than own teleconference verbs directly.

options.title: Defer the primitive
options.body: Leave current sessions_send and agent --deliver primitives as the supported path until multi-agent product direction is clearer.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow core design first
recommendation.body: Define the smallest core lifecycle API, SQLite or named-artifact storage model, transcript policy, and tests before inviting an implementation PR.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already provided the strongest maintainer-scoping review and appears in current history for the relevant agent/session surfaces.
